newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed at cancellation of Cobra deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed at cancellation of Cobra deal.

text.p: U.S. officials expressed disappointment Wednesday at Turkey's decision to cancel an order for U.S. Cobra helicopters but said they would continue to strive for a "sound" military relationship with Ankara.
"We're disappointed. We wanted to go forward with the sale," said one State Department official. "We're not blaming the Turkish government at all."

The sale of the 10 helicopters, manufactured by Textron Inc's Bell Helicopter, had been held up in the U.S. Congress by a coalition of Democrats and Republicans worried the gunships would be used against Kurdish rebels in Turkey.
"We work very hard with the Congress. It's not always possible to win the battles," the U.S. official said.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington had "worked very hard with the Turkish government on this military transfer. We and the Turks thought it was the right thing to do for Turkey, to enhance Turkey's security."

Despite the cancellation, "we will go forward in other ways to be a good ally to Turkey, to make sure that we have a military relationship that is sound and that meets the needs of both Turkey and the United States," Burns said.
Burns said the United States remained committed to a separate deal to sell Turkey four frigates, which is currently under discussion with Congress.

"We hope that some of the problems encountered (with the Cobras) will not have a negative effect on Turkey's willingness to consider U.S. military goods and U.S. military hardware and software to improve Turkey's defense capabilities," he said.
